top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards the optical lattice clock, with Katori's magic-wavelength scheme and Ye's realisation at 1e-18, a demonstrated and independently confirmed measurement advance. JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST and SYRTE agree in direct frequency-ratio comparisons, and the instrument now resolves millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and constrains drifts of constants and dark-matter couplings. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation rests on demonstrated performance, not on the prospective redefinition of the second, so it does not re-award the comb or ion-control prizes.
recusal_note: Spent a year of PhD in John Hall's lab (2005 comb laureate, not a credited name in P001); WACQT leadership overlaps institutionally with Chalmers; rare-earth-crystal quantum-memory work is adjacent to NV-centre and circuit-QED candidates. No tie to Katori or Ye.
